messages:
eng-monitor: ALERT: high tail latency on streaming endpoints (p99 spike)
eng-monitor: https://metrics.redwood.internal/alerts/5100012345 — streaming.p99 > 2.5s for 5m, error-rate + routing-latency increase :rotating_light:
eng-monitor: affected models: redwood/open-16k-v2 (heavy), traffic region: us-west-2, estimate ~0.8% of global requests
Alice Chen: grabbing it. oncall: @Mateo Ruiz are you around?
Mateo Ruiz: here, looking. initial glance shows p95 up from 180ms -> 420ms, p99 spiking to ~2.8s. streaming stalls (clients seeing blank frames) coincident with a compile-pipeline change 20m ago (compile-linker: incremental-linking=true) :thinking_face:
Priya Nair: saw a deploy event from buildfarm ~20m ago, "incremental-linker" flip. deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T11:02 UTC in prod/compile-pipeline job id 289312
deploy-bot: Rollout summary: compile-pipeline:v3.4.1 -> v3.5.0 (flag: incremental-linker=true)
Mateo Ruiz: collecting kernel logs from a hotbox. small reproducer shows decode step sometimes stalls on page allocation in kernel_linker when sequence > 2048 tokens. logs: ```
[2026-03-15 11:08:12] WARN kernel_linker: pagefault_count=187 latency_ms=1400
[2026-03-15 11:08:13] ERROR decode: tail-stall detected, kv-cache insert blocked
```
Mateo Ruiz: root cause hypothesis: incremental linker changes altered compile ordering, generating a kernel variant that interacts poorly with FlashAttention/TRT8 fused kernels causing occasional synchronous pagefaults under streaming continuous-batch workloads
Alice Chen: customer impact? any paid tenants affected? pinging customer-ops
customer-ops: immediate callback from AcmeAnalytics (high-volume streaming); they reported increased 5xxs and client-side stalls starting ~11:05 UTC. CS is triaging.
Priya Nair: quick mitigation options: 1) rollback compile-pipeline flag (fast) 2) temporarily route streaming traffic to older kernel variant in runtime routing policy (slower but zero-compiles) 3) apply a runtime patch to disable the fused kernel for long sequences (risky)
Mateo Ruiz: I can do (2) now — create a routing rule to force models matching open-16k-v2 to use kernel-variant:stable-202602. That should drop p99 back immediately without a full pipeline rollback
Alice Chen: do we have a safe canary for routing change? small percentage first
Mateo Ruiz: yes, I'll canary 5% in us-west-2 -> 50% in 3m -> 100% if healthy. command: ```
# runtime-cli route update --model open-16k-v2 --expr "region=='us-west-2' and path=='/stream'" --kernel stable-202602 --canary 5
```
eng-monitor: NOTE: rolling routing change will register as config-change; alerting may fluctuate
Priya Nair: while that's rolling, pls open rollback PR for compile-pipeline flag. I'll coordinate with buildfarm to block further rollouts of v3.5.0
Mateo Ruiz: applied canary at 11:18 UTC. metrics: after 2 min p99 in canary saw drop from 2.8s -> 190ms. pushing to 50% now.
eng-monitor: telemetry: overall p99 reduced from 2.8s -> 350ms after 50% rollout (still above baseline but trending). p95 back to ~220ms
SRE Shift: I'm putting a temporary capacity cushion on dedicated pools to avoid cascading timeouts (scale +10% on pool-128g-gpu)
deploy-bot: buildfarm: paused pipeline v3.5.0 job id 289312 — new schedules blocked.
Priya Nair: PR opened to flip incremental-linker=false and tag v3.5.1-rollfix, request: @Alice Chen review for quick rollback
Alice Chen: reviewing now. Also let's update the incident doc with customer impact notes and SLA risk
customer-ops: AcmeAnalytics: saw 3x increase in request latency and reported degraded model outputs. They're on a reserved plan; CS escalated to AE. Logged incident ref ACME-2026-0315
Mateo Ruiz: after 100% routing to stable kernel at 11:26 UTC, p99 returned to baseline ~180-220ms. I/O pagefaults in kernel logs dropped by 95%
eng-monitor: ALERT RESOLVED: streaming.p99 back under threshold for 10m, closing auto-alert window
Alice Chen: good mitigation. next steps: 1) fully revert compile-pipeline flag in prod (PR merged) 2) run full compile/validation locally to ensure no silent perf regressions 3) follow-up postmortem and release notes 4) notify impacted customers and schedule RCA call with AcmeAnalytics
Priya Nair: PR merged at 11:35 UTC, buildfarm triggered v3.5.1 rollback job 289400. We'll canary new compiled artifacts to verify no performance regressions before full re-enable of incremental-linker
SRE Shift: leaving a watch for the next 2h on p95/p99, will escalate if p99 rises above 500ms again. Pager in rotation: @SRE Shift -> next oncall in 2h
pagerduty-bot: Incident acknowledged by Alice Chen (oncall). Pager duty incident ID PD-67321 created and assigned to eng-runtime oncall
Alice Chen: handoff notes for next shift: timeline + commands executed + rollback PR #512 (flip incremental-linker=false) + routing change ID rc-2026-11 applied -> reverted when stable kernel rolled out. Runbook: if p99>500ms -> immediate rollback of routing (runtime-cli route update --revert rc-2026-11) then escalate to kernel-dev team.
Mateo Ruiz: logging snippet and authz to reproduce given in incident doc. I'll attach kernel traces and minimal replay harness to the ticket
customer-ops: Notifying AcmeAnalytics that mitigation applied and we are scheduling RCA for 11:00 UTC tomorrow. CS will follow up on compensation if SLA breached
Alice Chen: closing thread for live mitigation. we'll keep watch and record lessons: avoid flipping linker flags without canary across compile farm; add a perf regression gate for streaming p99 in CI. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
